tei:titleStmt.tei:title: הַנּוֹתֵן תְּשׁוּעָה
Prayer for the Royal Family of Peter II, King of Yugoslavia (1938)

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer for the Royal Family of Peter II, King of Yugoslavia (1938)

tei:lg.tei:l: Prayer for the King and the Fatherland
Almighty God, Lord of the universe!
You, who give power to rulers and glory to kings,
whose Kingdom is the kingdom of all ages,
You, who delivered David, Your servant, from all dangers,
who rules over sea and land,
bless and keep, save and sustain
our ruler
His Majesty, Peter II, King of Yugoslavia
Her Majesty, the Queen Mother Maria
and the entire illustrious House of Karađorđević
Grant, O God,
a long life to our king,
and remove from him all care and adversity.
[May he subdue nations beneath his sway,
and make his enemies fall before him;
and in every enterprise in which he shall engage may he prosper.]
[May the supreme King of kings
in his mercy place in his heart
and in the hearts of all his counselors,
a spirit of wisdom and understanding
to do good for our country
and for all of Yisrael.]
Bless him with the love of his subjects,
and let justice and peace reign under his scepter,
and may the borders of our land be constant and firm.
Bless, good God, our homeland,
the Kingdom of Yugoslavia,
that it may flourish and prosper,
and may joy fill all its citizens.
Grant that abundance of all blessings
may be bestowed upon us all!
[In his days and in ours
may Yehudah be saved
and Yisrael dwell in safety
and may the Redeemer come unto Ẓíōn]
So may Your will be done!

tei:note.tei:p: Peter II Karađorđević (Serbo-Croatian: Петар II Карађорђевић, Petar II Karađorđević; 6 September 1923 – 3 November 1970) was the last King of Yugoslavia, reigning from October 1934 until he was deposed in November 1945. He was the last reigning member of the Karađorđević dynasty.

Marija Karađorđević (6 January 1900 – 22 June 1961), Princess of Romania, was Queen of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes from 1922 to 1929 and Queen of Yugoslavia from 1929 to 1934 as the wife of King Alexander I. Her parents were Prince Ferdinand of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen (later Ferdinand I of Romania) and Princess Marie of Edinburgh (later Queen Maria). She was the mother of King Peter II. Her citizenship was revoked, and her property was confiscated by the Yugoslav communist regime in 1947, but she was posthumously rehabilitated in 2014.

The House of Karađorđević or Karađorđević dynasty (Serbian: Династија Карађорђевић, Dinastija Karađorđević, IPA: [karadʑǒːrdʑevitɕ]; pl. Карађорђевићи, Karađorđevići) is the former ruling Serbian and deposed Yugoslav royal family. During its existence, the dynasty intermarried with royal houses of Petrović-Njegoš, Romanov, Hohenzollern, Oldenburg, Baden, Hesse, Leiningen, Savoy, Liechtenstein and Orléans.
The Kingdom of Yugoslavia was a country in Southeast and Central Europe that existed from 1918 until 1941.
